preemption.details: California does not have statewide preemption for knife laws. Local municipalities (e.g., Los Angeles, San Francisco) may enact stricter knife ordinances than state law.

open_carry.details: California has no general prohibition on openly carrying knives. Fixed-blade knives must be carried in a sheath worn openly suspended from the waist to avoid being classified as concealed. Folding knives may be carried openly without restriction.

statutes.title: Openly worn sheath knife not concealed

concealed_carry.details: Concealed carry depends on the type of knife. Folding knives (non-locking and locking) may generally be carried concealed. Dirks, daggers, and fixed-blade knives cannot be concealed. A 'dirk or dagger' is broadly defined as any knife or instrument capable of ready use as a stabbing weapon that may inflict great bodily injury or death.

blade_length.details: California does not impose a statewide blade length limit. However, local ordinances may restrict blade length (e.g., Los Angeles restricts concealed carry of knives with blades over 3 inches).

switchblade.details: Switchblades with a blade of 2 inches or longer are illegal to carry on the person, possess in the passenger or driver area of a vehicle in a public place, sell, or transfer. Switchblades with a blade shorter than 2 inches are not prohibited under this section.

automatic.details: Automatic knives fall under the switchblade definition in California. If the blade is 2 inches or longer and opens automatically, it is illegal.

assisted_opening.details: Assisted-opening knives are not prohibited under California law. The switchblade definition (§ 17235) explicitly excludes knives that open with thumb pressure on the blade or a thumb stud, provided the knife has a detent or mechanism that resists opening or biases the blade toward its closed position.

statutes.title: Definition of switchblade knife (exclusion for assisted-opening)

ballistic_knife.details: Ballistic knives are prohibited under both federal law and California Penal Code.

restricted_locations.summary: Schools (K-12 and colleges), government buildings, courts, airports, and other locations as defined by statute.
restricted_locations.details: It is illegal to bring any knife with a blade longer than 2.5 inches onto K-12 school grounds (§ 626.10). Knives with blades over 4 inches are prohibited in state or local public buildings and at required-open public meetings (§ 171b).

statutes.title: Weapons in state or local public buildings
